name: Laurel Ring
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: A thick, heavy cast champagne-gold ring with a laurel wreath engraved on its flat face and crisp bevelled edges, modelled on the Ringed Dial ring.
good: The closest to the Ringed Dial ring you liked: weighty, classic and clearly legendary; it reads well at 1:1 because the ring is solid rather than lacy.
watch: Plainer than Jade Lode's open leaf scrolls; on its own it can read a little like a medal.

name: Reed Ring
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: A gold ring wrapped in overlapping low-relief river reeds and slender leaves, the high points polished by wear.
good: The most organic gold of the four and the most specific to the riverside; airy and elegant, closest in spirit to Jade Lode.
watch: Came out as an open wreath rather than a thick ring; the leaves reach slightly past the ring onto the status tray's top-left corner; the palest gold of the set.

name: Jade-set Band
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: A thick, smooth gold band set with four small jade cabochons at the compass points, with a fine beaded inner rim.
good: Ties the gold and the jade together most directly; jewellery-like craftsmanship; very clean silhouette.
watch: The four stones at the compass points make it read a little like a porthole or compass; the most regular and least organic ring.

name: Rooted Ring
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: A gold ring whose lower half breaks into fine gold roots that spread into the jade and grip it, as if the ring grew into the rock.
good: The most original idea: it merges Rootbound's 'grown into the corner' feel with Jade Lode's gold-in-jade; very organic.
watch: The ring itself came out thin rather than thick; the fine roots are busy at 1:1 and blur together.

name: River Granite
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: The jade becomes a water-worn grey river granite boulder with feldspar speckles and small cushions of moss.
good: The calmest and most natural rock; the moss ties it to Overgrown Relic; the grey lets the gold ring stand out clearly.
watch: Grey steps away from the green Gildmoss palette; the least precious-feeling material.

name: Gold-Quartz Slate
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: Dark layered slate with natural seams of white quartz carrying threads of native gold.
good: The most convincing 'ore' of the set: gold appears exactly as it does in a real vein; dark and dramatic, and the gold ring echoes the gold in the rock.
watch: The white quartz seams are high contrast and compete with the portrait; the most visually loud corner.

name: Star Iron
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: Meteoritic iron ('star metal') with the natural criss-cross crystal pattern on polished faces and a pitted natural crust.
good: The metal option you asked for, with a legendary story (metal that fell from the sky); cool steel-grey makes the gold warmer by contrast.
watch: The crystal pattern came out as a blocky embossed grid that looks manufactured and close to the faceted look rejected for the world's art.

name: Malachite
before_label: Jade Lode, the design it varies
change: Polished green malachite with concentric light and dark bands, breaking into a rough raw edge at the screen edges.
good: Stays green like the jade but with a striking natural banding; precious and organic.
watch: A brighter, more saturated emerald than the dark Gildmoss greens; the bands are busy behind the ring.
